steps.text:
1. Describe what the animal smells like.
It smells damp and fishy, a bit like seaweed that’s washed up on the beach, but maybe a bit more meaty.

2. Describe what the animal feels like to touch.
If you stroke it in one direction, it feels cold and smooth and damp. But in the other direction, it feels rough like sandpaper.

3. Describe how the animal moves.
It glides smoothly, its whole body snaking from side to side. Sometimes it moves slowly and sometimes it suddenly bursts forward.

4. Describe how the animal sounds.
This creature moves as silently as a ghost. You wouldn’t want to hear the crunch of its powerful jaws.

5. Describe where the animal lives.
Sunshine ripples down into the cool, blue, salty water. Sometimes it is smooth and calm, and other times it is stormy and rough.
In this example, we haven’t shown any of the guesses because we wanted to show the whole description. If the other player guesses after the first description, it stops there!

text:
How to Play:

Think of an animal and describe it to the other person using the five steps below. For each step, the other person is allowed to make one guess. The sooner they guess, the more points you get!

1. Describe what the animal smells like.
    You can use as many words as you like (but don’t say what the animal is). Don’t worry if you don’t know what it really smells like – imagine how it might smell.
    5 points
  2. Describe what the animal feels like to touch.
    You can use as many words as you like (but remember not to say what it looks like).
    4 points
  3. Describe how the animal moves.
    You can use as many words as you like (but don’t say what the animal is).
    3 points
  4. Describe how the animal sounds.
    You can use as many words as you like (but try not to make the actual noise).
    2 points
  5. Describe where the animal lives.
    You can use as many words as you like (but don’t say the place name, just say what the place is like).
    1 point
    If they don’t guess correctly, you can tell them the answer!


When the other player has guessed what your animal is, swap over so they can have a go at describing. Repeat a few times and see if you can improve your scores!
